structures.name: Scalp / head surface
structures.function: Translucent scalp for spatial context. Fiducials (nasion, LPA, RPA, Cz) sit on this surface in the 10–20 frame.
structures.clinical: Used here as an orientation shell, not as a surgical scalp model.

structures.name: Left cerebral cortex
structures.function: Neocortex: six-layered sheet folded into gyri and sulci. It is the seat of perception, action, language and association.
structures.clinical: Focal lesions produce highly local signs (aphasia, neglect, hemiparesis) that map onto Brodmann / gyral anatomy.

structures.name: Right cerebral cortex
structures.function: Neocortex: six-layered sheet folded into gyri and sulci. It is the seat of perception, action, language and association.
structures.clinical: Focal lesions produce highly local signs (aphasia, neglect, hemiparesis) that map onto Brodmann / gyral anatomy.

structures.name: Midbrain (mesencephalon)
structures.function: Rostral brainstem: tectum (colliculi), tegmentum (red nucleus, SN, reticular formation) and cerebral peduncles. Cranial nerves III–IV exit here.
structures.clinical: Midbrain strokes (Weber, Benedikt, Parinaud) combine oculomotor signs with corticospinal or cerebellar findings.

structures.name: Superior colliculus
structures.function: Paired tectal hillocks for visuomotor orienting and the vertical gaze pathways (posterior commissure / riMLF).
structures.clinical: Compression at the tectal plate (pineal mass) yields Parinaud syndrome: upgaze palsy and light-near dissociation.

structures.name: Inferior colliculus
structures.function: Auditory midbrain nucleus: almost all ascending brainstem auditory fibres synapse here before the MGN.
structures.clinical: Lesions can impair sound localisation and, rarely, cause auditory hallucinations or palatal myoclonus circuits nearby.

structures.name: Pons
structures.function: Basilar pons carries corticospinal and corticopontine fibres; the tegmentum holds CN V–VIII nuclei, the locus coeruleus and pontine reticular formation.
structures.clinical: Pontine infarcts (locked-in, Millard–Gubler) and central pontine myelinolysis are classic clinical correlates.

structures.name: Medulla oblongata
structures.function: Caudal brainstem: pyramids, olives, and the vital cardiorespiratory reticular networks. CN IX–XII nuclei live here.
structures.clinical: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) and medial medullary syndromes are teaching staples; medullary compression is life-threatening.

structures.name: Left cerebral peduncle
structures.function: Crus cerebri: compact corticospinal and corticobulbar fibres on the ventral midbrain.
structures.clinical: Weber syndrome: ipsilateral III palsy plus contralateral hemiparesis from a peduncular infarct.

structures.name: Right cerebral peduncle
structures.function: Crus cerebri: compact corticospinal and corticobulbar fibres on the ventral midbrain.
structures.clinical: Weber syndrome: ipsilateral III palsy plus contralateral hemiparesis from a peduncular infarct.

structures.name: Left medullary pyramid
structures.function: Corticospinal tract on the ventral medulla; ~90% of fibres decussate at the pyramidal decussation to form the lateral CST.
structures.clinical: Medial medullary (Dejerine) syndrome hits the pyramid, medial lemniscus and hypoglossal nerve.

structures.name: Right medullary pyramid
structures.function: Corticospinal tract on the ventral medulla; ~90% of fibres decussate at the pyramidal decussation to form the lateral CST.
structures.clinical: Medial medullary (Dejerine) syndrome hits the pyramid, medial lemniscus and hypoglossal nerve.

structures.name: Left inferior olivary nucleus
structures.function: Climbing-fibre source to cerebellar Purkinje cells; central to motor timing and learning.
structures.clinical: Olivary hypertrophy after central tegmental-tract lesions is linked to palatal (and sometimes ocular) myoclonus.

structures.name: Right inferior olivary nucleus
structures.function: Climbing-fibre source to cerebellar Purkinje cells; central to motor timing and learning.
structures.clinical: Olivary hypertrophy after central tegmental-tract lesions is linked to palatal (and sometimes ocular) myoclonus.

structures.name: Left red nucleus
structures.function: Midbrain tegmental nucleus on the dentatorubrothalamic and rubrospinal paths. Drawn as a labelled schematic ellipsoid — it is not in the open mesh sets.
structures.clinical: Claude and Benedikt syndromes involve the red nucleus with cerebellar tremor and oculomotor palsy.

structures.name: Right red nucleus
structures.function: Midbrain tegmental nucleus on the dentatorubrothalamic and rubrospinal paths. Drawn as a labelled schematic ellipsoid — it is not in the open mesh sets.
structures.clinical: Claude and Benedikt syndromes involve the red nucleus with cerebellar tremor and oculomotor palsy.

structures.name: Left cerebral white matter
structures.function: Myelinated association, commissural and projection axons that wire cortex to cortex and to subcortex.
structures.clinical: Leukoaraiosis, MS plaques and watershed infarcts preferentially hit this compartment.

structures.name: Right cerebral white matter
structures.function: Myelinated association, commissural and projection axons that wire cortex to cortex and to subcortex.
structures.clinical: Leukoaraiosis, MS plaques and watershed infarcts preferentially hit this compartment.

structures.name: Corpus callosum
structures.function: The great commissure: genu, body, splenium (and rostrum) interconnecting homologous cortical fields.
structures.clinical: Callosal disconnection (alien-hand, left anomia for objects in the left hand) and agenesis are classic teaching cases.

structures.name: Fornix
structures.function: Main hippocampal output arching under the corpus callosum to the mammillary bodies (Papez circuit).
structures.clinical: Fornix damage (colloid cyst surgery, trauma) can produce severe anterograde amnesia.

structures.name: Left internal capsule
structures.function: Compact projection bundle (anterior limb, genu, posterior limb) between caudate/thalamus and lentiform nucleus.
structures.clinical: A small lacunar infarct in the posterior limb can cause a dense contralateral hemiparesis.

structures.name: Right internal capsule
structures.function: Compact projection bundle (anterior limb, genu, posterior limb) between caudate/thalamus and lentiform nucleus.
structures.clinical: A small lacunar infarct in the posterior limb can cause a dense contralateral hemiparesis.

structures.name: Left optic tract
structures.function: Post-chiasmatic retinal axons heading for the lateral geniculate nucleus.
structures.clinical: A tract lesion yields contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

structures.name: Right optic tract
structures.function: Post-chiasmatic retinal axons heading for the lateral geniculate nucleus.
structures.clinical: A tract lesion yields contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

structures.name: Left thalamus
structures.function: Relay and association nuclei that gate almost every subcortical input to cortex (except olfaction).
structures.clinical: Thalamic strokes produce hemisensory loss, pain (Déjerine–Roussy), aphasia or neglect depending on the territory.

structures.name: Right thalamus
structures.function: Relay and association nuclei that gate almost every subcortical input to cortex (except olfaction).
structures.clinical: Thalamic strokes produce hemisensory loss, pain (Déjerine–Roussy), aphasia or neglect depending on the territory.

structures.name: Left intralaminar thalamus (CM/Pf)
structures.function: Centromedian / parafascicular complex — the thalamic target of the dorsal ARAS route, projecting widely to cortex and striatum.
structures.clinical: Intralaminar lesions and DBS targets are discussed in disorders of consciousness and Tourette syndrome.

structures.name: Right intralaminar thalamus (CM/Pf)
structures.function: Centromedian / parafascicular complex — the thalamic target of the dorsal ARAS route, projecting widely to cortex and striatum.
structures.clinical: Intralaminar lesions and DBS targets are discussed in disorders of consciousness and Tourette syndrome.

structures.name: Left pulvinar
structures.function: Large posterior association nucleus linking visual and attentional cortical networks.
structures.clinical: Pulvinar damage is associated with spatial neglect and visual-attention deficits.

structures.name: Right pulvinar
structures.function: Large posterior association nucleus linking visual and attentional cortical networks.
structures.clinical: Pulvinar damage is associated with spatial neglect and visual-attention deficits.

structures.name: Left lateral geniculate nucleus
structures.function: Thalamic visual relay: magno- and parvocellular laminae project via optic radiations to V1.
structures.clinical: LGN lesions cause incongruous homonymous field cuts.

structures.name: Right lateral geniculate nucleus
structures.function: Thalamic visual relay: magno- and parvocellular laminae project via optic radiations to V1.
structures.clinical: LGN lesions cause incongruous homonymous field cuts.

structures.name: Left medial geniculate nucleus
structures.function: Thalamic auditory relay to Heschl’s gyrus.
structures.clinical: Rare isolated lesions can impair auditory discrimination.

structures.name: Right medial geniculate nucleus
structures.function: Thalamic auditory relay to Heschl’s gyrus.
structures.clinical: Rare isolated lesions can impair auditory discrimination.

structures.name: Hypothalamus
structures.function: Homeostatic and endocrine brain: autonomic, circadian, thermoregulatory, appetitive and pituitary-control nuclei. The ventral ARAS route traverses here.
structures.clinical: Hypothalamic lesions disturb sleep, temperature, appetite, water balance and endocrine axes.

structures.name: Tuberomammillary nucleus (histamine)
structures.function: Sole neuronal histamine source. A key waking node on the ventral ARAS path; antihistamines that cross the BBB cause drowsiness here.
structures.clinical: TMN inhibition is a target of some hypnotics; narcolepsy circuits interact with this wake-promoting cell group.

structures.name: Pituitary gland
structures.function: Adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis in the sella, under hypothalamic releasing-hormone and ADH/oxytocin control.
structures.clinical: Adenomas cause endocrine syndromes and bitemporal hemianopia from chiasmal compression.

structures.name: Pineal gland
structures.function: Epithalamic endocrine gland secreting melatonin; sits above the tectal plate in the quadrigeminal cistern.
structures.clinical: Pineal masses obstruct the aqueduct (hydrocephalus) and compress the superior colliculi (Parinaud).

structures.name: Basal forebrain (incl. nucleus basalis)
structures.function: Cholinergic waking and memory node (nucleus basalis of Meynert, medial septum, diagonal band) — the cortical end of the ventral ARAS route.
structures.clinical: Degenerates early in Alzheimer disease; anticholinergic burden impairs attention and memory.

structures.name: Left caudate nucleus
structures.function: Striatal nucleus hugging the lateral ventricle; associative and oculomotor loops dominate in the head of caudate.
structures.clinical: Atrophies in Huntington disease; caudate infarcts can cause abulia or choreiform movements.

structures.name: Right caudate nucleus
structures.function: Striatal nucleus hugging the lateral ventricle; associative and oculomotor loops dominate in the head of caudate.
structures.clinical: Atrophies in Huntington disease; caudate infarcts can cause abulia or choreiform movements.

structures.name: Left putamen
structures.function: Lentiform striatum, heavily sensorimotor; with the caudate it forms the input stage of the basal ganglia.
structures.clinical: Putaminal haemorrhage (hypertension) is a common deep ICH; lacunar infarcts cause lacunar syndromes.

structures.name: Right putamen
structures.function: Lentiform striatum, heavily sensorimotor; with the caudate it forms the input stage of the basal ganglia.
structures.clinical: Putaminal haemorrhage (hypertension) is a common deep ICH; lacunar infarcts cause lacunar syndromes.

structures.name: Left globus pallidus externa
structures.function: Indirect-pathway node: GABAergic projection to STN. Shapes the brake on movement.
structures.clinical: Pallidal lesions and DBS alter dystonia and dyskinesia circuits.

structures.name: Right globus pallidus externa
structures.function: Indirect-pathway node: GABAergic projection to STN. Shapes the brake on movement.
structures.clinical: Pallidal lesions and DBS alter dystonia and dyskinesia circuits.

structures.name: Left globus pallidus interna
structures.function: Major basal-ganglia output to motor thalamus (and brainstem). High tonic inhibition is paused to release a selected action.
structures.clinical: GPi DBS is a standard treatment for dystonia and a Parkinson option.

structures.name: Right globus pallidus interna
structures.function: Major basal-ganglia output to motor thalamus (and brainstem). High tonic inhibition is paused to release a selected action.
structures.clinical: GPi DBS is a standard treatment for dystonia and a Parkinson option.

structures.name: Left nucleus accumbens
structures.function: Ventral striatum: reward, motivation and Pavlovian–instrumental interface, heavily innervated by VTA dopamine.
structures.clinical: Implicated in addiction, depression and apathy; a target in experimental DBS.

structures.name: Right nucleus accumbens
structures.function: Ventral striatum: reward, motivation and Pavlovian–instrumental interface, heavily innervated by VTA dopamine.
structures.clinical: Implicated in addiction, depression and apathy; a target in experimental DBS.

structures.name: Left subthalamic nucleus
structures.function: Glutamatergic pacemaker of the indirect pathway, sitting on the midbrain–diencephalon border.
structures.clinical: STN lesions cause hemiballismus; STN DBS is a mainstay for Parkinson motor fluctuations.

structures.name: Right subthalamic nucleus
structures.function: Glutamatergic pacemaker of the indirect pathway, sitting on the midbrain–diencephalon border.
structures.clinical: STN lesions cause hemiballismus; STN DBS is a mainstay for Parkinson motor fluctuations.

structures.name: Left substantia nigra
structures.function: SNc dopaminergic neurons pigmented with neuromelanin; SNr is a GABAergic output nucleus akin to GPi.
structures.clinical: SNc degeneration is the core pathology of Parkinson disease.

structures.name: Right substantia nigra
structures.function: SNc dopaminergic neurons pigmented with neuromelanin; SNr is a GABAergic output nucleus akin to GPi.
structures.clinical: SNc degeneration is the core pathology of Parkinson disease.

structures.name: Left amygdala
structures.function: Basolateral and central nuclei for threat detection, Pavlovian fear and the autonomic emotional response.
structures.clinical: Klüver–Bucy (bilateral) and Urbach–Wiethe (basolateral calcification) are classic human lesions.

structures.name: Right amygdala
structures.function: Basolateral and central nuclei for threat detection, Pavlovian fear and the autonomic emotional response.
structures.clinical: Klüver–Bucy (bilateral) and Urbach–Wiethe (basolateral calcification) are classic human lesions.

structures.name: Left hippocampus
structures.function: Allocortical memory engine (CA fields, dentate, subiculum) essential for episodic encoding and spatial maps.
structures.clinical: Mesial temporal sclerosis → temporal-lobe epilepsy; early atrophy is a hallmark of Alzheimer disease.

structures.name: Right hippocampus
structures.function: Allocortical memory engine (CA fields, dentate, subiculum) essential for episodic encoding and spatial maps.
structures.clinical: Mesial temporal sclerosis → temporal-lobe epilepsy; early atrophy is a hallmark of Alzheimer disease.

structures.name: Left cerebellar hemisphere
structures.function: Cerebrocerebellum: planning, timing and coordination of skilled movement via dentate → VL thalamus → cortex.
structures.clinical: Hemispheric lesions cause ipsilateral limb dysmetria, intention tremor and dysdiadochokinesia.

structures.name: Right cerebellar hemisphere
structures.function: Cerebrocerebellum: planning, timing and coordination of skilled movement via dentate → VL thalamus → cortex.
structures.clinical: Hemispheric lesions cause ipsilateral limb dysmetria, intention tremor and dysdiadochokinesia.

structures.name: Cerebellar vermis
structures.function: Midline cerebellum for axial and gait coordination and some vestibulo-oculomotor control.
structures.clinical: Vermian lesions (medulloblastoma, alcohol) produce truncal ataxia and titubation.

structures.name: Left dentate nucleus
structures.function: Largest deep cerebellar nucleus; output of the cerebellar hemispheres.
structures.clinical: Dentate involvement appears in some degenerative ataxias and in cerebellar outflow tremor.

structures.name: Right dentate nucleus
structures.function: Largest deep cerebellar nucleus; output of the cerebellar hemispheres.
structures.clinical: Dentate involvement appears in some degenerative ataxias and in cerebellar outflow tremor.

structures.name: Left lateral ventricle
structures.function: C-shaped CSF space (frontal, body, atrium, temporal and occipital horns) lined by ependyma and containing choroid plexus.
structures.clinical: Enlarges in hydrocephalus and atrophy; temporal horns balloon early in obstructive hydrocephalus.

structures.name: Right lateral ventricle
structures.function: C-shaped CSF space (frontal, body, atrium, temporal and occipital horns) lined by ependyma and containing choroid plexus.
structures.clinical: Enlarges in hydrocephalus and atrophy; temporal horns balloon early in obstructive hydrocephalus.

structures.name: Third ventricle
structures.function: Midline slit between the thalami, with choroid in the roof and the hypothalamic recesses on the floor.
structures.clinical: Colloid cysts at the foramen of Monro can cause sudden obstructive hydrocephalus.

structures.name: Cerebral aqueduct
structures.function: Sylvius’ aqueduct through the midbrain, linking third and fourth ventricles.
structures.clinical: Aqueductal stenosis is a classic cause of triventricular hydrocephalus.

structures.name: Fourth ventricle
structures.function: Diamond-shaped CSF space between pons/medulla (floor) and cerebellum (roof); outlets are the foramina of Luschka and Magendie.
structures.clinical: Floor lesions produce cranial-nerve and gaze findings; obstruction → hydrocephalus.

structures.name: Left internal carotid artery
structures.function: Terminal ICA in the subarachnoid space, giving rise to MCA, ACA and the posterior communicating artery.
structures.clinical: ICA stenosis and terminus aneurysms are major stroke and SAH sources.

structures.name: Right internal carotid artery
structures.function: Terminal ICA in the subarachnoid space, giving rise to MCA, ACA and the posterior communicating artery.
structures.clinical: ICA stenosis and terminus aneurysms are major stroke and SAH sources.

structures.name: Left middle cerebral artery
structures.function: Sylvian artery supplying lateral convexity, basal ganglia (lenticulostriates) and the sensorimotor face/arm territories.
structures.clinical: The most common large-vessel ischaemic stroke territory.

structures.name: Right middle cerebral artery
structures.function: Sylvian artery supplying lateral convexity, basal ganglia (lenticulostriates) and the sensorimotor face/arm territories.
structures.clinical: The most common large-vessel ischaemic stroke territory.

structures.name: Left anterior cerebral artery
structures.function: Runs in the interhemispheric fissure, supplying medial frontal and parietal cortex including the leg area of homunculus.
structures.clinical: ACA stroke: contralateral leg weakness, abulia and grasp phenomena.

structures.name: Right anterior cerebral artery
structures.function: Runs in the interhemispheric fissure, supplying medial frontal and parietal cortex including the leg area of homunculus.
structures.clinical: ACA stroke: contralateral leg weakness, abulia and grasp phenomena.

structures.name: Anterior communicating artery
structures.function: Short link between the two ACAs that completes the anterior Circle of Willis.
structures.clinical: The single most common site of saccular aneurysm.

structures.name: Left posterior cerebral artery
structures.function: Terminal basilar branches to occipital lobe, medial temporal lobe and (via perforators) thalamus and midbrain.
structures.clinical: PCA stroke: contralateral hemianopia, and alexia without agraphia if the splenium is included on the left.

structures.name: Right posterior cerebral artery
structures.function: Terminal basilar branches to occipital lobe, medial temporal lobe and (via perforators) thalamus and midbrain.
structures.clinical: PCA stroke: contralateral hemianopia, and alexia without agraphia if the splenium is included on the left.

structures.name: Left posterior communicating artery
structures.function: Links ICA to PCA and can fetalise the posterior circulation when large.
structures.clinical: PCom aneurysms classically present with ipsilateral III palsy.

structures.name: Right posterior communicating artery
structures.function: Links ICA to PCA and can fetalise the posterior circulation when large.
structures.clinical: PCom aneurysms classically present with ipsilateral III palsy.

structures.name: Basilar artery
structures.function: Midline vessel formed by the vertebrals, running along the clivus/pons to bifurcate into the PCAs.
structures.clinical: Basilar occlusion can produce locked-in syndrome or coma from ARAS and corticospinal destruction.

structures.name: Left vertebral artery
structures.function: Paired arteries that enter the foramen magnum and join to form the basilar; they give PICA.
structures.clinical: Vertebral dissection and PICA infarcts (including Wallenberg) are common posterior-circulation events.

structures.name: Right vertebral artery
structures.function: Paired arteries that enter the foramen magnum and join to form the basilar; they give PICA.
structures.clinical: Vertebral dissection and PICA infarcts (including Wallenberg) are common posterior-circulation events.

structures.name: Superior sagittal sinus
structures.function: Unpaired dural venous sinus in the attached edge of falx cerebri, draining convexity veins to the confluence of sinuses.
structures.clinical: CVT here causes headache, papilloedema and sometimes bilateral parasagittal infarcts or haemorrhage.

structures.name: Left transverse sinus
structures.function: Runs in the tentorium to the sigmoid sinus and jugular bulb.
structures.clinical: Often asymmetric (right-dominant); thrombosis mimics chronic headache and raised ICP.

structures.name: Right transverse sinus
structures.function: Runs in the tentorium to the sigmoid sinus and jugular bulb.
structures.clinical: Often asymmetric (right-dominant); thrombosis mimics chronic headache and raised ICP.

structures.name: Left olfactory nerve (I)
structures.function: Fila olfactoria through the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb and tract. Special visceral afferent for smell.
structures.clinical: Anosmia after trauma or meningioma of the olfactory groove; uncinate seizures produce olfactory auras.

cn.name: Olfactory
cn.nucleus: Olfactory bulb (telencephalic, not a true brainstem nerve)

structures.name: Right olfactory nerve (I)
structures.function: Fila olfactoria through the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb and tract. Special visceral afferent for smell.
structures.clinical: Anosmia after trauma or meningioma of the olfactory groove; uncinate seizures produce olfactory auras.

cn.name: Olfactory
cn.nucleus: Olfactory bulb (telencephalic, not a true brainstem nerve)

structures.name: Left optic nerve (II)
structures.function: CNS tract from globe through the optic canal to the chiasm. Myelinated by oligodendrocytes.
structures.clinical: Papilloedema, optic neuritis and field cuts are localised by the classic chiasmal rules.

cn.name: Optic
cn.nucleus: Retinal ganglion cells → LGN (not a brainstem nucleus)

structures.name: Right optic nerve (II)
structures.function: CNS tract from globe through the optic canal to the chiasm. Myelinated by oligodendrocytes.
structures.clinical: Papilloedema, optic neuritis and field cuts are localised by the classic chiasmal rules.

cn.name: Optic
cn.nucleus: Retinal ganglion cells → LGN (not a brainstem nucleus)

structures.name: Left oculomotor nerve (III)
structures.function: Innervates MR, SR, IR, IO and levator; parasympathetic pupilloconstrictor fibres ride on its surface.
structures.clinical: A “down and out” eye with ptosis and a blown pupil suggests a compressive III (PCom aneurysm, herniation).

cn.name: Oculomotor
cn.nucleus: Oculomotor nucleus and Edinger–Westphal, midbrain tegmentum

structures.name: Right oculomotor nerve (III)
structures.function: Innervates MR, SR, IR, IO and levator; parasympathetic pupilloconstrictor fibres ride on its surface.
structures.clinical: A “down and out” eye with ptosis and a blown pupil suggests a compressive III (PCom aneurysm, herniation).

cn.name: Oculomotor
cn.nucleus: Oculomotor nucleus and Edinger–Westphal, midbrain tegmentum

structures.name: Left trigeminal nerve (V)
structures.function: Great sensory nerve of the face plus muscles of mastication. Three divisions: V1, V2, V3.
structures.clinical: Trigeminal neuralgia (often vascular compression at the REZ) and herpes zoster ophthalmicus are common.

cn.name: Trigeminal
cn.nucleus: Principal, mesencephalic, spinal V and motor V nuclei

structures.name: Right trigeminal nerve (V)
structures.function: Great sensory nerve of the face plus muscles of mastication. Three divisions: V1, V2, V3.
structures.clinical: Trigeminal neuralgia (often vascular compression at the REZ) and herpes zoster ophthalmicus are common.

cn.name: Trigeminal
cn.nucleus: Principal, mesencephalic, spinal V and motor V nuclei

structures.name: Left facial nerve (VII)
structures.function: Muscles of facial expression, taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, and several parasympathetic secretomotor fibres.
structures.clinical: LMN VII (Bell) vs UMN (forehead sparing) is a core localisation drill. CPA tumours can involve VII with VIII.

cn.name: Facial
cn.nucleus: Facial nucleus (pontine tegmentum) and superior salivatory nucleus

structures.name: Right facial nerve (VII)
structures.function: Muscles of facial expression, taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, and several parasympathetic secretomotor fibres.
structures.clinical: LMN VII (Bell) vs UMN (forehead sparing) is a core localisation drill. CPA tumours can involve VII with VIII.

cn.name: Facial
cn.nucleus: Facial nucleus (pontine tegmentum) and superior salivatory nucleus

structures.name: Left vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII)
structures.function: Special somatic afferent for hearing and balance, from cochlea and labyrinth through the IAM to the CPA.
structures.clinical: Vestibular schwannoma: progressive unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus and later V/VII involvement.

cn.name: Vestibulocochlear
cn.nucleus: Cochlear and vestibular nuclei at the pontomedullary junction

structures.name: Right vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII)
structures.function: Special somatic afferent for hearing and balance, from cochlea and labyrinth through the IAM to the CPA.
structures.clinical: Vestibular schwannoma: progressive unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus and later V/VII involvement.

cn.name: Vestibulocochlear
cn.nucleus: Cochlear and vestibular nuclei at the pontomedullary junction

structures.name: Left vagus nerve (X)
structures.function: The wanderer: palate, pharynx, larynx, and parasympathetic supply to thoracic and abdominal viscera.
structures.clinical: Unilateral X: hoarseness and palatal droop; bilateral lesions threaten the airway and autonomic control.

cn.name: Vagus
cn.nucleus: Nucleus ambiguus and dorsal motor nucleus of X, medulla

structures.name: Right vagus nerve (X)
structures.function: The wanderer: palate, pharynx, larynx, and parasympathetic supply to thoracic and abdominal viscera.
structures.clinical: Unilateral X: hoarseness and palatal droop; bilateral lesions threaten the airway and autonomic control.

cn.name: Vagus
cn.nucleus: Nucleus ambiguus and dorsal motor nucleus of X, medulla

structures.name: Left locus coeruleus (NE)
structures.function: Pontine noradrenergic nucleus that broadcasts novelty, stress and gain control across cortex and thalamus.
structures.clinical: LC degeneration is early in Alzheimer and Parkinson disease and is linked to arousal and autonomic instability.

structures.name: Right locus coeruleus (NE)
structures.function: Pontine noradrenergic nucleus that broadcasts novelty, stress and gain control across cortex and thalamus.
structures.clinical: LC degeneration is early in Alzheimer and Parkinson disease and is linked to arousal and autonomic instability.

structures.name: Dorsal raphe (5-HT)
structures.function: Midline serotonergic cell group in the ventral PAG / dorsal midbrain, modulating mood, sleep and pain.
structures.clinical: A target of SSRIs; midbrain haemorrhage can injure this cluster with the PAG.

structures.name: Median raphe (5-HT)
structures.function: More caudal serotonergic raphe projecting heavily to hippocampus and cortex; part of the ventral arousal stream.
structures.clinical: Together with the dorsal raphe it sets a serotonergic tone implicated in anxiety and sleep architecture.

structures.name: Periaqueductal grey
structures.function: Grey matter around the aqueduct: defensive behaviour, descending pain control, and a hub of the dorsal arousal path.
structures.clinical: PAG lesions (and stimulation) alter pain, autonomic state and, in some reports, consciousness.

structures.name: Left parabrachial complex
structures.function: Pontine relay for visceral, taste and interoceptive afferents; a recently emphasised node for arousal and affective state.
structures.clinical: PBN injury is discussed in coma and in the affective dimension of pain.

structures.name: Right parabrachial complex
structures.function: Pontine relay for visceral, taste and interoceptive afferents; a recently emphasised node for arousal and affective state.
structures.clinical: PBN injury is discussed in coma and in the affective dimension of pain.

structures.name: Left pedunculopontine tegmental nucleus (ACh)
structures.function: Cholinergic mesopontine nucleus (PPT / PTg) projecting to thalamus — a pillar of the dorsal ARAS route and of gait/locomotor pattern generation.
structures.clinical: PPN DBS has been tried for Parkinsonian gait freezing; degeneration occurs in progressive supranuclear palsy.

structures.name: Right pedunculopontine tegmental nucleus (ACh)
structures.function: Cholinergic mesopontine nucleus (PPT / PTg) projecting to thalamus — a pillar of the dorsal ARAS route and of gait/locomotor pattern generation.
structures.clinical: PPN DBS has been tried for Parkinsonian gait freezing; degeneration occurs in progressive supranuclear palsy.

structures.name: Left laterodorsal tegmental nucleus (ACh)
structures.function: Sister cholinergic cell group to PPN, contributing ACh to thalamus and to REM-on networks.
structures.clinical: Part of the mesopontine cholinergic system that fragments in synucleinopathies.

structures.name: Right laterodorsal tegmental nucleus (ACh)
structures.function: Sister cholinergic cell group to PPN, contributing ACh to thalamus and to REM-on networks.
structures.clinical: Part of the mesopontine cholinergic system that fragments in synucleinopathies.

structures.name: Mesencephalic reticular formation
structures.function: Core midbrain reticular field that integrates ascending sensory drive and projects to intralaminar thalamus.
structures.clinical: A strategic lesion here (or in both paramedian thalami) is a classic cause of coma.

structures.name: Nucleus pontis oralis
structures.function: Rostral pontine reticular nucleus on both the ascending arousal path and descending locomotor/REM circuits.
structures.clinical: Pontine tegmental lesions that include PnO can abolish REM sleep and impair arousal.

structures.name: Ventral tegmental area (DA)
structures.function: Midbrain dopamine neurons projecting to nucleus accumbens, prefrontal cortex and amygdala — motivation and the ventral arousal stream.
structures.clinical: Drugs of abuse converge on VTA→NAc; VTA lesions blunt reward seeking.

structures.name: Left eyeball
structures.function: Schematic globe at a roughly MNI-consistent orbit. Real extraocular muscles are not modelled.
structures.clinical: Orbit pathology is not the focus of this page; use it as a landmark for CN II / III.

structures.name: Right eyeball
structures.function: Schematic globe at a roughly MNI-consistent orbit. Real extraocular muscles are not modelled.
structures.clinical: Orbit pathology is not the focus of this page; use it as a landmark for CN II / III.

structures.name: Left lens (schematic)
structures.function: Schematic lens sitting in the anterior globe.
structures.clinical: Cataract and accommodation are outside the scope of this neuroanatomy page.

structures.name: Right lens (schematic)
structures.function: Schematic lens sitting in the anterior globe.
structures.clinical: Cataract and accommodation are outside the scope of this neuroanatomy page.

structures.name: Left cochlea (schematic)
structures.function: Schematic spiral of Corti — not a segmented temporal-bone reconstruction.
structures.clinical: Sensorineural hearing loss localises to hair cells, spiral ganglion or CN VIII.

structures.name: Right cochlea (schematic)
structures.function: Schematic spiral of Corti — not a segmented temporal-bone reconstruction.
structures.clinical: Sensorineural hearing loss localises to hair cells, spiral ganglion or CN VIII.

structures.name: Left semicircular canals (schematic)
structures.function: Three schematic rings (horizontal, anterior, posterior) standing in for the bony labyrinth.
structures.clinical: Canal paresis and BPPV are localised here; this geometry is labelled schematic, not a CT segmentation.

structures.name: Right semicircular canals (schematic)
structures.function: Three schematic rings (horizontal, anterior, posterior) standing in for the bony labyrinth.
structures.clinical: Canal paresis and BPPV are localised here; this geometry is labelled schematic, not a CT segmentation.

structures.name: Left olfactory epithelium (schematic)
structures.function: Schematic patch on the cribriform region where olfactory receptor neurons sit.
structures.clinical: Viral and traumatic anosmia often begin at this epithelium or the fila through the cribriform plate.

structures.name: Right olfactory epithelium (schematic)
structures.function: Schematic patch on the cribriform region where olfactory receptor neurons sit.
structures.clinical: Viral and traumatic anosmia often begin at this epithelium or the fila through the cribriform plate.

structures.name: Midbrain axial section
structures.function: Placeholder for a PittBrains3D midbrain axial plate (colliculi, PAG, red nucleus, SN, peduncles).
structures.clinical: Use the slice presets to clip the solid brainstem at this level when the real plate is not loaded.

structures.name: Pontine axial section
structures.function: Placeholder for a pontine axial plate (basilar pons, tegmentum, CN nuclei, fourth-ventricle floor).
structures.clinical: Exploded view fans the plates apart along the brainstem axis.

structures.name: Rostral medulla axial section
structures.function: Placeholder for a rostral medullary plate (olives, inferior cerebellar peduncles, hypoglossal eminence).
structures.clinical: Compare with the caudal plate to see the opening of the fourth ventricle.

structures.name: Caudal medulla axial section
structures.function: Placeholder for a caudal medullary plate (pyramids, medial lemniscus, decussation approaching).
structures.clinical: This is the level of several medial vs lateral medullary stroke cartoons.

structures.name: Cerebral arteries
structures.function: Combined anterior and posterior cerebral arterial tree (Pitt print mesh).
structures.clinical: Useful for circle-of-Willis context; named branches are not separated in this build.

structures.name: Cerebral veins
structures.function: Superficial and deep cerebral veins as a single mesh.
structures.clinical: Vein of Galen / internal cerebral veins are not labelled separately.

structures.name: Dural sinuses and reflections
structures.function: Dural venous sinuses and falx/tentorium reflections.
structures.clinical: Individual sinus names stay in the tree as folders until split meshes exist.

structures.name: Cranial nerves (Pitt bundle)
structures.function: Combined cranial-nerve rootlets after the brainstem component was removed.
structures.clinical: Named CN I–XII are not separable in the source STL.

structures.name: Tongue
structures.function: Oral tongue for spatial context with the oral cavity and lower cranial nerves.
structures.clinical: Not a surgical mucosa model.

structures.name: Optic chiasm
structures.function: Decussation of nasal retinal fibres; sits above the pituitary.
structures.clinical: Compression here produces bitemporal hemianopia.

credits.title: Sources and licences
credits.disclaimer: Positions are template-based (MNI152) and many meshes in this build are schematic placeholders. Vessels, nerves and nuclei from different donors will not sit in a single true anatomy. Do not use this page for clinical localisation.

items.name: Allen Human Reference Atlas 3D via Human Reference Atlas
items.note: Cortical, subcortical, ventricular, cerebellar and brainstem backbone.

items.name: PittBrains3D
items.note: Cranial nerves, cerebral vessels, dural sinuses and brainstem axial sections. Share-alike applies to derived meshes.

items.name: Harvard Ascending Arousal Network Atlas v2.0
items.note: AAN nuclei (LC, raphe, PAG, PBN, PPN, LDTg, MRF, PnO, VTA).

items.name: BodyParts3D
items.note: Gap-fillers such as pituitary, pineal and inferior colliculus when present.

items.name: fsaverage head / 10–20 fiducials
items.note: Translucent scalp context and nasion / LPA / RPA / Cz.

items.name: Procedural sensory organs
items.note: Eyeball, lens, cochlea, semicircular canals and olfactory epithelium when no open mesh exists. Always labelled schematic.
